subtitle: Design organisations, complex B2B products and AI transformation made concrete.

bio.short: I lead design as an organisation and as a working part of product delivery. At Ninox I owned the design function's capacity, allocation, structure and development; at Datameer I led UX across Germany and New York. Today at Bibel TV I turn AI into shipped workflows, new product experiences and executable prototypes.
bio.long:
At Ninox I sat on the Senior Leadership Team. I owned the design function's operating model across product design and UX writing: capacity, allocation, prioritisation, team structure and processes. I built levelling and growth structures, hired two and promoted two. For four months I also led product, bringing the scope to nine people across two functions and four disciplines.

At Datameer I led UX across Germany and New York for five years. The product was data-dense enterprise analytics for regulated banks and insurers. During a new-product bet, research gained executive backing and design moved into roadmap conversations. I built the screening method that reached analysts inside institutions standard panels could not access.

At Bibel TV I work directly at the AI and delivery layer. I prototype against real APIs with Claude Code, and the external engineering agency works from the running software. I shipped a human-controlled Microsoft Copilot workflow for viewer support and built an AI fundraising workflow from performance analysis through production skill. The throughline is making systems usable: the organisation designers work in, the complex product a customer works in, or the internal workflow software can improve.

context.emphasis: Lead with design-organisation ownership at Ninox, distributed complex-B2B leadership at Datameer and working AI systems at Bibel TV. Use workflow productisation as the connection to 4flow's operational software portfolio.
